title: Electric Protocol
glossary: In the document, the term CERs refers to all behind the meter generating and storage technology
In the document, the term Consumer Participant (CP) is used to refer to homes or businesses connected to the grid

questions.text: Retail banks and/or government agencies offer customers no or low interest home energy efficiency loans or rebates to customers for behind-the-meter technology or other energy efficiency investments

rubric.label: No low cost finance available. Finance is equivalent to normal lending
Some low cost finance available but not yet universally acessible
Special loans or rebates available to reduce upfront cost and available to all customers

questions.text: Affordability and accessibility across society

rubric.label: behind-the-meter technology only affordable and accessible to highest earners
behind-the-meter technology only affordable and accessible to middle and highest earners
behind-the-meter technology affordable and accessible to all earners inc. through zero capital cost models

questions.text: Cost of finance at rates to scale technology

rubric.label: Cost of finance only available at or above 10%
Cost of finance for behind-the-meter technology above 5% and below 10%
Cost of finance for behind-the-meter technology available at or below 5%

questions.text: Statewide best practices for calculating and communicating benefits from behind-the-meter technology to customers including self-consumption, generation and market value

rubric.label: No universal best practices or standards in place
Best practices and standards in place for consumer protection but not enforced
Best practices and standards in place for consumer protection and are enforced

questions.text: Network and system operators can own and operate behind-the-meter technology (within a free market with other possible owners)

rubric.label: Network operators face significant barriers to operating, incentivising, contracting with or owning behind-the-meter technology
Network operators face some barriers to operating, incentivising, contracting with or owning behind-the-meter technology
Network operators face no barriers to operating, incentivising, contracting with or owning behind-the-meter technology

questions.text: Marketplace with open transparent time-of-day pricing for electricity import/consumption for all customers.

rubric.label: No time of use pricing for electricity import in place for customers
Time of use pricing for electricity import available to some customers
Time of use pricing for electricity import available to all or almost all customers

questions.text: Marketplace with open transparent time-of-day pricing for electricity export for all customers.

rubric.label: No export pricing available
Export pricing available but restricted to only one form of behind-the-meter technology or not available to all customers
Time of use pricing available for export to all customers and both solar and storage

questions.text: All electricity bills include a breakdown of all charges that add up to the net payment or bill.

rubric.label: Bills are not broken down into constituent parts – only one cost/tariff shown
Bills broken down to show all of the following: wholesale/energy costs, network costs, system operation and taxes (where these are applicable)

questions.text: Half hour (or better) meter data is available to support accurate design of behind-the-meter technology

rubric.label: Data is not available
Data can be obtained through a manual process
Data is available in an electronic fomat online

questions.text: No barriers to participation for behind-the-meter technology in energy and ancillary markets based on asset size or technology

rubric.label: behind-the-meter technology have size barriers in all wholesale and ancillary markets
behind-the-meter technology have size barriers 50% or more of the wholesale and ancillary markets which are open to behind-the-meter technology
No size barriers for behind-the-meter technology in more than  50% of the wholesale and ancillary markets which are open to behind-the-meter technology

questions.text: Ancillary and wholesale market pricing is publicly available

rubric.label: At least one wholesale or ancillary market does not have transparent pricing
All ancillary  and wholesale markets pricing is fully transparent
All ancillary  and wholesale markets pricing is fully transparent, and pricing is available in real time

questions.text: behind-the-meter technology or customers can participate individually or in Virtual Power Plants

rubric.label: VPPs are not allowed in any wholesale or ancillary market
VPPs have access to no more than 50% of wholesale or ancillary markets which are open to behind-the-meter technology
VPPs have access to more than 50% of wholesale or ancillary markets which are open to behind-the-meter technology

questions.text: Market signals for behind-the-meter technology and customers to contribute to network reinforcement and network capacity i.e. provide grid and network infrastructure investment deferral

rubric.label: No compensation available
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards but only under trials
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards as part of business as usual

questions.text: Voltage regulation, voltage stabilty and voltage imbalance

rubric.label: No compensation available / market does not exist for any assets.
Compensation available but not to all customers
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards for all customers.

questions.text: Frequency regulation, keeping and reserves including spinning/non-spinning reserve

rubric.label: No compensation available / market does not exist for any assets.
Compensation available but not to all customers
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards for all customers.

questions.text: Peak demand reduction including demand charge reduction

rubric.label: No compensation available / market does not exist for any assets.
Compensation available but not to all customers
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards for all customers.

questions.text: Compensation for reducing demand or increasing generation during periods of high wholesale pricing (i.e. responding to tight supply conditions)

rubric.label: No compensation available / market does not exist for any assets.
Compensation available but not to all customers
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards for all customers.

questions.text: Black Start

rubric.label: No compensation available / market does not exist for any assets.
Compensation available but not to all customers
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards for all customers.

questions.text: Demand increase

rubric.label: No compensation available / market does not exist for any assets.
Compensation available but not to all customers
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards for all customers.

questions.text: Demand response (downturn)

rubric.label: No compensation available / market does not exist for any assets.
Compensation available but not to all customers
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards for all customers.

questions.text: Carbon

rubric.label: No compensation available / market does not exist for any assets.
Compensation available but not to all customers
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards for all customers.

questions.text: Any other non-wholesale market available to other generators

rubric.label: No compensation available / market does not exist for any assets.
Compensation available but not to all customers
Compensation available to all behind-the-meter technology that meet required technical standards for all customers.

questions.text: Zero cost for self-consuming electricity generation from behind the meter behind-the-meter technology

rubric.label: A fee is payable by customers to anyone involved in the grid, network, system, or other power system incumbent to connect behind-the-meter technology behind the meter
A fee is payable but only to a standards or certification body
No fee is payable

questions.text: No regulatory barriers to customers for connecting behind-the-meter technology for self-consumption

rubric.label: customers not allowed to connect behind-the-meter technology even if for self-consumption
No barriers to connecting and using behind-the-meter technology for self-consumption

questions.text: Simple online asset registration or standard automated permitting process to replace any local permitting requirements

rubric.label: Permitting is required before a behind-the-meter technology can be installed and is complex or risky to obtain
Permitting is required but is simple and online
Fit and inform, or no permitting in place

questions.text: Planning rules and building codes do not unnecessarily restrict installation of behind-the-meter technology and enable net zero

rubric.label: planning and / or building rules impose cost or restrictions on solar / battery install
planning rules apply to restrict installation in certain locations
solar panel installs are permitted activities and building consents only apply to rooftop arrays above certain sizes

questions.text: Zero cost, standardised, and transparent automated interconnection/grid connection process for all customers and behind-the-meter technology

rubric.label: Interconnection application always required before a behind-the-meter technology can be installed and is complex,costly or time consuming to obtain
Interconnection application is required but is simple and online.  Applications are processeed in less than 15 days.
Fit and inform, or no permitting in place (size restrictions permitted only for export to the grid)

questions.text: Open publicly available map or data of capacity for import and export across all networks so that all users know what they can connect.

rubric.label: No database of capacity on networks
There is a database of network capacity, but it is not open to the public or does not show individual customers
There is a full location specific database of available capacity for customers to connect behind-the-meter technology

questions.text: Transparent and publicly available cost/payment for increasing import and export capacity

rubric.label: No publicly available data
Data available but is only for import or export or some customers
Data available for import and export at all connection points/all customers

questions.text: Simple and digital registration of behind-the-meter technology with utilities

rubric.label: No registration process
Registration process but is paper based
Digital registration process in place which is at least regionalised

questions.text: Grid and system operators have the correct incentives in place for technology (e.g. grid forming batteries) which operate the power system with behind the meter technology, including dispatching the grid with at least 70% of total electrical supply coming from behind the meter sources

rubric.label: System operator cannot dispatch with more than 20% of total electricity generation from behind the meter tech at any one time
System operator cannot dispatch with more than 50% of total electricity generation from behind the meter tech at any one time
System operator can dispatch with more than 70% of total electricity generation from behind the meter at any one time

questions.text: System operators set or approve technical and communication protocols for behind-the-meter technology market participation at  national level

rubric.label: Localised technical and communication protocols
Some localised rules and some national/statewide rules
National and universally adopted rules which also confirm to international norms

questions.text: System operators set or approve technical and communication protocols for behind-the-meter technology data exchange at state or national level

rubric.label: Localised technical and communication protocols
Some localised rules and some national/statewide rules
National and universally adopted rules which also confirm to international norms

questions.text: Statewide best practices for electrical and mechanical installation

rubric.label: No universal best practices or standards in place
Best practices and standards in place which are continually (at least annually) reviewed and align to international best

questions.text: Statewide best practices for safety

rubric.label: No universal best practices or standards in place
Best practices and standards in place which are continually (at least annually) reviewed and align to international best practice

questions.text: No tariffs charged at border on behind-the-meter technology

rubric.label: Tariffs on imported behind-the-meter technology >=25%
Tariffs on imported behind-the-meter technology >=10% <25%
Tariffs on imported behind-the-meter technology <10%

questions.text: Tax rebates/subsidies to customers for behind-the-meter technology or other energy efficiency investments

rubric.label: tax incentives or subsides available to utility scale technology or other energy technology are more valuable than those provided to behind-the-meter technology.
any tax incentives or subsidies for behind-the-meter technology at least match those provided to utility scale technology or other energy technology

questions.text: Statewide standardised curriculum and qualifications for behind-the-meter technology installers and maintainers

rubric.label: No standard recognised qualification
National qualification certificate(s) for behind-the-meter technology installation and maintenance

questions.text: Access to training courses to achieve recognised behind-the-meter technology installation and maintenance qualifications

rubric.label: No courses offered
Course offered but in single location or infrequently (>6 monthly)
Courses offered throughout country and on a regular basis
